metadata.title: security: Replace os.system() with shutil.rmtree() in run_mutmut.py
metadata.author: mango766

description:
## Summary

The `os.system()` call in `run_mutmut.py` executes commands through the shell without proper input validation, which could pose a security risk if command arguments were influenced by external input.

## Changes

- Replace `os.system("rm -rf mutants .mutmut-cache")` with `shutil.rmtree()`
- Remove unused `import os`
- Add `import shutil` for safe directory removal
- Document the remaining `shell=True` usage in `run_command()` (these are internal commands constructed by the script, not from external input)

## Impact

- 1 file changed
- 4 insertions, 2 deletions
- Removes shell command execution risk from directory cleanup

This follows the pattern used elsewhere in the project for file system operations and aligns with security best practices (avoiding `os.system()` and `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` when possible).

commits.message:
fix: use parameterized query to prevent SQL injection in cleanup_old_results

Replace f-string SQL query with parameterized query using '?' placeholder
to prevent potential SQL injection when days_old parameter comes from
untrusted input.

Closes #3898

commits.message:
fix: only catch FileNotFoundError in run_mutmut.py cleanup

Replace ignore_errors=True with a targeted try/except FileNotFoundError
so that real errors (PermissionError, OSError, etc.) propagate instead
of being silently swallowed. This prevents the script from proceeding
with stale mutant data when directory removal actually fails.

Also updates the differential test suite:
- Verifies rmtree is called without ignore_errors
- Adds test that PermissionError propagates (not swallowed)
- Updates docstrings to match new behavior

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti
